newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens wins 29 million DM tram order.
newsitem.headline: Siemens wins 29 million DM tram order.

text.p: German electronics giant Siemens AG said on Tuesday its transportation unit and Adtranz received a 29 million mark ($18.2 million) order for trams for the Belgian cities of Antwerp and Ghent.
The order is for nine trams due to go into service in the autumn of 1998, and includes an option for 36 more vehicles.
Siemens will provide control system and electrical technology. Adtranz, a venture of Germany's Daimler Benz AG and the Swiss-Swedish group ABB, would be responsible for drive technology.
A third supplier, Deutsche Waggonbau AG, will manufacture mechanical portions of the trans.
The trams feature low floors to provide easy access for passengers in wheelchairs or with baby carriages. Similar trams are already in service in Germany in Dresden and Mannheim.

In December, Siemens said its transportation unit would likely show a loss in the 1996-97 business year as a result of price competition for contracts and high start-up costs for several rail projects.
